vik: FYI ran a long soak with nvme-staging enabled and a new offload-throttle patch. hit a weird regression: steady-state looks fine but during tenant handoff storms we see long request stalls and occasional OOMs.

anya: can you share the patch link and the exact config?

vik: patch in my branch `offload-throttle-win` (WIP). config used: ```
offload.throttle_tokens=100
offload.reclaim_window_ms=50
soft_reserve_dynamic=enabled
nvme.staging.priority=hot
coalesce.defer_threshold=0.6
```

leo: interesting. what's throttle_tokens semantics? is it per-shard or global?

vik: current impl is global token bucket for the node. each offload/reclaim consumes tokens; tokens refill at rate proportional to free_staging_bytes. it was meant to prevent stampeding offloads.

ciara: stampeding control sounds right, but global bucket might be unfair across tenants. a noisy tenant can hog tokens and starve others -> stalls -> timeouts. We should consider per-tenant or per-shard credits.

vik: we saw exactly that. Tenant B (high kv-cache churn) consumed >80% tokens during a burst. Tenant A got delayed, grew resident working set, and then OOMed when compactor couldn't keep up.

anya: two axes to explore: (1) per-tenant min-guarantee + max-burst, (2) async backpressure path where stalled offloads fall back to recompute/evict decisions rather than blocking request threads.

leo: +1. Also add a low-watermark fast-path: when staging_free < low_watermark, offload should switch to light-weight remap/alias strategy (defer full copy/coalesce) to avoid staging pressure.

vik: I like that. prototype added `alias_remap_only` mode. But gotcha: remap leaves multiple virtual aliases which complicates compaction later. need to tag such ranges for later cleanup.

ciara: make sure to track `alias_pending_compact` flags and a separate background scanner that compacts when staging_free recovers. otherwise we'll accumulate alias debt.

anya: telemetry items we need: `throttle_tokens_used_per_tenant`, `reclaim_window_latency_ms`, `alias_pending_bytes`, `staging_free_bytes`, `per_shard_reclaim_credits`. without those we can't tune.

evict-bot: scheduled perf run: `offload-throttle-win` on canary group #3, run id 482.

leo: another edge case: NVMe IO amplification. remap -> compact later causes double write of same data to nvme which hurts throughput and wear. maybe prefer in-memory transient staging (host-pinned) when latency-sensitive and nvme busy. needs cost model.

vik: agreed. we should expose `prefer_host_staging_when_nvme_iops>X` or better, dynamic policy that queries nvme_iops and staging_free. also consider a per-tenant cost budget to avoid overusing host memory.

ciara: also watch for page ownership races: during remap we temporarily have aliases in two shards. if a request tries to mutate a page, we need copy-on-write semantics or strong pin checks. otherwise data corruption.

anya: suggested mitigation: while alias_remap_only is active mark remapped pages read-only and instrument COW on write path. it's heavier but safe. set heuristics to disable remap for write-heavy slabs.

vik: perf numbers from canary so far: baseline tokens/sec dropped ~3% but OOM events went from 5/day to 0 in that window. p99 latency improved in heavy-frag runs by ~40ms.

leo: seems like tradeoff is acceptable for Dedicated/Private, maybe not for Hosted low-latency tiers. Add runtime tier knob and sane defaults.

ciara: action items: (1) switch token bucket to per-tenant credits with min guaranteed and burst window, (2) implement `alias_pending_compact` scanner, (3) add COW write-path for remapped pages, (4) telemetry metrics as @anya listed, (5) policy to prefer host staging when NVMe iops high.

vik: i'll open a follow-up PR with per-tenant credits and telemetry today, and add design notes for COW remap. cc @anya @leo for review.

anya: i'll try to run a multitenant noisy neighbor stress tomorrow. @evict-bot please schedule smoke run after PR lands.

evict-bot: enqueue job: `smoke-multitenant-offload` pending PR merge.

leo: thanks all. this helps with fairness + durability tradeoffs. keep notes on expected cost (nvme writes, host mem usage) so we can document defaults in the console.
